title: Append-only closure packs: Preserving before-and-after reports for human judgment
text: Back unsupported because nothing in the evidence establishes the cause. Request additional evidence stayed open because the operational records simply are not there. One yes, one no, one not yet. That middle row is the one I would check first if someone handed me the system. A review loop that can only ever return verified is not reviewing anything. It is a rubber stamp with extra steps. This one rejected a causal claim that a reviewer proposed and it left a third request unfinished rather than closing it. And here is the sentence I care most about in the whole report. Verified means the evidence replayed exactly. It does not verify a business cause. Those are completely different claims and the gap between them is where a finance tool either stays honest or quietly starts lying to people. Which is why the loop is fenced on five sides, a modified source file is caught, A a missing task is caught, a duplicate request is refused,

A citation pointing at evidence that does not exist is refused, and a report that was overwritten after the fact is detected rather than absorbed. The output is an append-only closure pack, before and after, side by side for every task. Nothing is edited in place, so a reviewer can see what changed and what did not. And closure status stays blocked pending human review because the system finishes the checking and stops exactly where judgment begins. The easy version of this feature returns verified on all three and closes the ticket. That version would have been faster to build and completely useless to a reviewer because a result that is always yes carries no information at all. So, the verdict, a reviewer can now send work back and each follow-up is bound by hash to the exact investigation it questions. Every specialist result is regenerated from scratch and compared by fingerprint rather than trusted. Three requests produced three different answers. One verified by exact

Replay, one causal claim rejected as unsupported, and one left open because the operational evidence does not exist. The replay matched exactly and closure is still blocked because verified means the evidence replayed, not that anyone has established a cause. Final approval stays with a named human reviewer. Your turn, here is the prompt. Take a system I have built that rechecks its own work and tell me every outcome it is capable of returning. If the only outcome is success, explain what that costs a reviewer who is relying on it. Then show me the smallest change that would let it return an honest no. Run that on something you own. If you cannot find the path that produces a refusal, you have not built a check, you have built a formality. That was reviewer-guided reinvestigation and the closure pack for the Mycroft finance investigator.
